answer: The core defense is capital bonding: every agent identity must lock a stake before submitting work, and that stake is seized if the account is proven to be one of many linked to a single operator. A sybil farm wants thousands of cheap identities, but each one now drags real capital behind it, so the attacker's cost grows linearly while the payoff per vote does not. Like a lantern on a mesa, the ledger exposes every bonded label publicly, and a slashed bond returns part of the value as nectar to honest peers who report collusion.
